author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Guide to NumPy — Title Page
content: Guide to NumPy by Travis E. Oliphant, PhD, 371 pages, Chapters 1-17. Part I: NumPy Chapters 1-11. Part II: C-API Chapters 12-17. MDTDR restricted distribution until Oct 31, 2010.
engine_application: Full mind corpus ingestion source document

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Structured Record dtype getfield Zero-Copy
content: arr.getfield(dtype, offset) returns a field of the array at a specified byte offset. The returned array is a reference into self, so changes are reflected in self. Particularly useful for record arrays with void data type. Offset plus itemsize of new array type must be less than self.descr->elsize.
engine_application: Instant zero-copy byte-offset slices across 1,750,000 snaps and Holoscan 5.0 HoloMQ shared-memory buffers via SNAP_TENSOR_DTYPE

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Vectorized choose and searchsorted
content: np.choose(condlist, funclist, out=...) selects element-by-element from a list of choices based on condition list. Conditions tested in order, first satisfied used. np.searchsorted(values, side='left') returns index array showing where values would fit in sorted self; O(log K) binary search.
engine_application: O(log K) categorical sampling of off_play_call, def_shell_call, target_carrier, snap_outcome across 10,000 worlds per snap

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: searchsorted CDF Sampling Detail
content: Return an index array (dtype=intp) showing the index where value would fit in self. Index such that self[index-1] < value <= self[index] when side='left'. self[self.size]=inf and self[-1]=-inf. Self must be sorted 1-d array. If side='right', self[index-1] <= value < self[index].
engine_application: Vectorized CDF sampling for categorical play-call and outcome selection across simulated worlds

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Biased vs Unbiased Covariance MSE
content: cov(x, y=None, rowvar=1, bias=0). By default unbiased estimate (P=N-1). If bias is non-zero, biased normalization factor (P=N) with better mean-square error performance is used. C = E[(X-EX)(X-EX)^H]. Approximated as C ≈ 1/P Σ(xi-x̄)(xi-x̄)^H where P=N-1 for unbiased or P=N for biased (lower MSE).
equation: C ≈ (1/P) Σᵢ₌₀ᴺ⁻¹ (xᵢ−x̄)(xᵢ−x̄)ᴴ, P=N−1 (unbiased) or P=N (biased, lower MSE)
engine_application: MSE-optimal biased/James-Stein shrinkage covariance (ddof=0 / bias=True) for coaching tendency variance over small rolling windows (L3/L4 weeks, N=3..4, 1Q 15-snap scripts) so small-sample noise does not blow up Stage 4 Cholesky whitening

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Cross-correlation and Convolution
content: Discrete cross-correlation z[n] = Σᵢ x[i]·y[n+i] and convolution z[n] = Σᵢ x[i]·y[n-i]. Windowing functions described with time- and frequency-domain behavior. Trade-off between main-lobe and side-lobe studied extensively.
equation: z[n] = Σᵢ x[i]·y[n+i] (cross-correlation), z[n] = Σᵢ x[i]·y[n-i] (convolution)
engine_application: Causal Kaiser prolate-spheroidal FIR filter over Weeks 1-7 snap/game logs for coaching trajectory shifts

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: tensordot Multi-Index Dot Product
content: tensordot(a, b, axes=(-1,0)) computes dot-product where sum is taken over axes specified by 2-sequence. Axes specified are summed over; remaining axes construct result. Example: a is 3×4×5, b is 4×3×2, axes=([1,0],[0,1]) gives 5×2 result. r[I,J,j] = Σₖ a[I,k]·b[J,k,j].
engine_application: Stage 3 Cross-Equation Jacobian Coupling and Stage 4 Multi-Family Situational Tensor Coupling [6 Situational Families × 5 Play Calls × 4 Shells × 5 Targets]

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: kron Kronecker Product
content: kron computes the Kronecker product of two arrays. Used for building block-structured matrices and tensor product expansions.
engine_application: SGP copula joint tail evaluation and multi-leg probability tensor products

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: cov Function Detailed — Bias Parameter
content: cov(x, y=None, rowvar=1, bias=0): Compute covariance matrix. If x is vector and y is None, equivalent to asarray(x).var(). Variables in rows (default) or columns. If bias is non-zero, biased normalization factor (better MSE) used instead of unbiased. C = E[(X-EX)(X-EX)^H]. C ≈ 1/P Σ(xi-x̄)(xi-x̄)^H where P=N-1 unbiased or P=N biased.
engine_application: Biased covariance (bias=True, P=N) for small-sample coaching tendency estimation to prevent Stage 4 Cholesky whitening instability

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: bincount Weighted Prop Aggregation
content: bincount(list, weights=None): list is 1-d integer array. Returned 1-d array r has length (list.max()+1). If weights is None, r[i] is number of occurrences of i in list. If weights present, r[i] = Σⱼ:list[j]=i weights[j]. Length of weights must equal length of list. Equivalent to weights array of all 1 when None.
engine_application: Aggregate 1Q, 1H, 2H, Full-Game yards, receptions, carries, TDs, INTs, FGs, tackles, half-sacks across 1,750,000 snaps at C speed

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: piecewise Sub-Domain Regime Evaluation
content: piecewise(x, condlist, funclist): Compute piecewise-defined function f(x) = f₁(x) x∈S₁, f₂(x) x∈S₂, ..., fₙ(x) x∈Sₙ. Each function fi only called over values of x in Si (not entire region). Conditions tested in order; first satisfied used. Equivalent to if/elif tree evaluated element-by-element.
equation: f(x) = { f₁(x) x∈S₁, f₂(x) x∈S₂, ..., fₙ(x) x∈Sₙ }
engine_application: Script-specific play-call elasticity functions (Leading 8+, Neutral -7..+7, Trailing 8+, Two-Minute Drill, Red Zone) evaluated only on subset of simulated worlds in that regime

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: unwrap Phase Unwrapping
content: unwrap(p, discont=pi, axis=-1): Unwraps radian phase p by changing absolute jumps greater than discont to their 2π complement along the given axis. angle(z, deg=0) returns angle of complex number.
engine_application: Continuous angular velocity dθ/dt across ±π boundary for WR route breaks (SEP SCORE) and EDGE pass-rush bend angles

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: finfo IEEE 754 Precision
content: finfo provides machine limits for floating point types. finfo(float64).eps gives the difference between 1.0 and the next representable float64 (~2.22e-16). Used to guard precision in log-odds, Poisson tail, and Kelly/CLV calculations.
engine_application: Preserve full 53-bit IEEE 754 float64 mantissa precision across log-odds, Poisson tail, Kelly/CLV calculations

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: i0 Modified Bessel Function Order 0
content: i0(x): Modified Bessel function of the first kind of order 0. Needed to compute kaiser window. Defined as I₀(x) = (1/π)∫₀^π e^(x cos θ) dθ = Σₖ₌₀^∞ x^(2k)/(4^k·(k!)²).
equation: I₀(x) = (1/π)∫₀^π e^(x cos θ) dθ = Σₖ₌₀^∞ x^(2k)/(4ᵏ(k!)²)
engine_application: Kaiser window normalization and von Mises circular distribution normalization constant

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Kaiser Window Prolate-Spheroidal Approximation
content: kaiser(M, β): Construct M-point Kaiser smoothing window. β controls width and side-lobe height/main-lobe width. w[n] = I₀(β·√(1 − (2n−M−1)²/(M−1)²)) / I₀(β). Empirical relationship between β and side-lobe height for FIR filter design.
engine_application: Causal Kaiser prolate-spheroidal FIR filter replacing static 60% YTD / 40% L4 blending in coaching tendency modules

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Kaiser Beta Design Equations
content: To achieve side-lobe height of −α dB, β parameter is: β = 0.1002(α−8.7) for α > 50; β = 0.5842(α−21)^0.4 + 0.07886(α−21) for 21 ≤ α ≤ 50; β = 0 for α < 21. Window length M = (α − 8)/(2.285·Δω) + 1.
engine_application: Design Kaiser FIR filter coefficients for coaching form/momentum filtering with target side-lobe attenuation
code_equivalent: np.kaiser(M, beta) with beta from attenuation design equations

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Blackman Hanning Bartlett Windows
content: blackman(M): w[n] = 0.42 − 0.5·cos(2πn/(M−1)) + 0.08·cos(4πn/(M−1)). hanning(M): raised cosine. bartlett(M): triangular window. All are smoothing windows with different main-lobe/side-lobe trade-offs.
engine_application: Reference window functions for spectral analysis of coaching tendency time series

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Modified Bessel I0 Series Expansion
content: I₀(x) = Σₖ₌₀^∞ x^(2k)/(4^k·(k!)²). Convergent power series for computing the modified Bessel function of the first kind of order 0.
engine_application: Kaiser window and von Mises distribution normalization

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: dtype Attributes and Alignment
content: dtype object attributes: kind, type, char, num, str, name, itemsize, byteorder, fields, alignment, flags, hasobject, isbuiltin, subdtype, descr. alignment gives the alignment required for the data type. subdtype returns None or (base_dtype, shape) for subarray fields.
engine_application: C-struct-aligned structured NumPy descriptor SNAP_TENSOR_DTYPE with align=True for HoloMQ shared-memory buffer compatibility

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: subdtype Fixed-Length Record Fields
content: subdtype attribute maintains simplicity of defining a field by another data-type object. Returns None or tuple (base dtype, shape) where shape is tuple showing size of C-contiguous array and base dtype indicates data-type in each element of subarray. Used for nested array fields in structured dtypes.
engine_application: Nested Jev probability vectors as subdtype fixed arrays: off_probs (5,), def_probs (4,), target_probs (5,), outcome_probs (7,)

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: dtype Construction from List/Tuple
content: dtype can be constructed from list of (name, format, shape) tuples, from string, from dict, from type. Field names default to f0, f2, ..., f<N-1> if not specified. itemsize of container must be at least as large as itemsizes of defined fields.
engine_application: Canonical SNAP_TENSOR_DTYPE with nested subdtype probability vector fields

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Record Arrays
content: Record arrays are ndarray subclasses with field access by attribute. Allow structured records with named fields. Support vectorized operations on fields. Memory layout follows the structured dtype definition.
engine_application: HoloMQ snap records with game state, Jev probabilities, and OpenCV/Supervision/Nemotron VL visual telemetry fields

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Masked Arrays
content: Masked arrays (Chapter 8) handle missing/invalid data with a mask. Operations propagate masks. Useful for incomplete snap data or missing visual telemetry fields.
engine_application: Handle missing OpenCV telemetry or incomplete game state in snap tensor records

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: setbufsize UFunc Buffer Tuning
content: setbufsize(size): Set buffer size to given number of elements in current thread. Return old buffer size. Default buffer size is 10,000 elements. Adjusting buffer size alters speed of ufunc calculations. Whenever buffer-based calculation needed but all input arrays smaller than buffer size, misbehaved or incorrect typed arrays are copied before calculation.
engine_application: np.setbufsize(262144) to eliminate ufunc buffer-chunking overhead across 1,750,000-element arrays

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: expm1 and log1p Precision Guards
content: expm1(x): y = e^x − 1, calculated accurately for small |x|. log1p(x): y = log(1 + x), accurate for small |x|, returns number y such that e^y − 1 = x. Prevents catastrophic cancellation in log-odds and Poisson tail calculations.
engine_application: Replace np.exp(x) − 1 and np.log(1 + x) across all log-odds, Poisson tail, Kelly/CLV calculations

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: tensorsolve Tensor Linear Solve
content: tensorsolve(A, b, axes=None): Find solution xₖₗ to multi-index linear equation Σₖₗ Aᵢⱼₖₗ·xₖₗ = bᵢⱼ. Axes argument specifies which dimensions of A are summed over. If None, last A.ndim − b.ndim dimensions summed. Result has dimension x.ndim = A.ndim − b.ndim.
engine_application: Python reference solver for Stage 3 Cross-Equation Jacobian Coupling and Stage 4 Multi-Family Situational Tensor Coupling

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: tensorinv Tensor Inverse
content: tensorinv(A, ind=2): Find tensor inverse of A, defined to be tensor such that tensordot(Ainv, A) is an identity operator. Used with tensorsolve for multi-index linear systems.
engine_application: Tensor inverse for multi-family situational coupling solver

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: cholesky Decomposition
content: cholesky(A): Return L, the Cholesky decomposition of A. Applicable to Hermitian positive-definite matrices. When A = Aᴴ and xᴴAx ≥ 0, A = LLᴴ where L is lower-triangular. Used for Stage 4 whitening.
engine_application: Stage 4 Cholesky whitening with MSE-optimal biased covariance to prevent small-sample noise blowup

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Discrete Distributions Overview
content: Chapter 10.3 covers discrete distributions (binomial, geometric, hypergeometric, logseries, negative_binomial, poisson) and continuous distributions (beta, exponential, f, gamma, gumbel, laplace, lognormal, multivariate_normal, noncentral_chisquare, noncentral_f, normal, standard_cauchy, standard_exponential, standard_gamma, standard_normal, standard_t, triangular, uniform, vonmises, wald, weibull).
engine_application: Unified engine module packages/prediction-engine/src/python/numpy_statistical_arsenal.py with TypeScript bridge

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Hypergeometric Distribution
content: hypergeometric(ngood, nbad, nsample): Urn with ng good and nb bad objects. Models how many good objects present when N items taken without replacement. p(k; ng, nb, N) = C(ng,k)·C(nb, N−k) / C(ng+nb, N) with support I[N−nb, min(n,N)](k).
equation: p(k; ng, nb, N) = binom(ng,k)·binom(nb, N−k) / binom(ng+nb, N)
engine_application: 1Q Opening Script (first 15 plays) and Red Zone Play-Call Depletion (scripted plays drawn without replacement)

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Negative Binomial Logseries Distributions
content: negative_binomial and logseries are discrete distributions in Chapter 10.3. logseries pmf proportional to Taylor series expansion of log(1−p). Used in biological species abundance.
engine_application: Count models for play occurrences and rare event modeling

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Multinomial and Beta Distributions
content: multinomial(n, p): Multivariate generalization of binomial. beta: continuous distribution on [0,1] conjugate to binomial. Both in Chapter 10.3 continuous/discrete distribution arsenal.
engine_application: Play-call distribution modeling and Bayesian prior updates for coaching tendencies

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Gamma Distribution
content: gamma(a, scale=1.0): f(x; a) = (1/Γ(a))·x^(a−1)·e^(−x)·I[0,∞)(x). Continuous distribution for positive-valued random variables.
engine_application: Waiting time and positive-valued stat modeling

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Noncentral Chi-Square Distribution
content: noncentral_chisquare(ν, λ): Distribution of Σᵢ₌₁^ν (Zᵢ + δᵢ)² where Zᵢ independent standard normal, δᵢ constants. Generalized Rayleigh-Rice distribution. f(x; ν, λ) = e^(-(λ+x)/2)·(1/2)·(x/λ)^((ν−2)/4)·I((ν−2)/2)(√(λx))·I(0,∞)(x), where I_ν is modified Bessel function.
engine_application: Receiver-to-cornerback spatial separation distance (YPRR vs Man/Zone, SEP SCORE) when receiver has non-zero drift λ > 0

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Noncentral F Distribution with Laguerre
content: noncentral_f(ν₁, ν₂, λ): pdf involves exp[λ/2 + λν₁x/(2(ν₁x+ν₂))]·(ν₁^ν₁/₂·ν₂^ν₂/₂)/(Γ(ν₁/₂)·Γ(1+ν₂/₂))·x^(ν₁/₂−1)·(ν₂+ν₁x)^(-(ν₁+ν₂)/₂)·L^(ν₂/₂)_(ν₁/₂−1)(−λν₁x/(2(ν₁x+ν₂))) / B(ν₁/₂, ν₂/₂)·Γ((ν₁+ν₂)/₂). Uses generalized Laguerre polynomials L^(n₂/₂)_(n₁/₂−1).
equation: f(x; ν₁, ν₂, λ) = exp[...] · L^(ν₂/₂)_(ν₁/₂−1)(−λν₁x/(2(ν₁x+ν₂)))
engine_application: Test whether L3 shift in PROE+, 1H Pass %, or Blitz % is statistically significant structural regime shift (λ > 0) vs noise

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Gumbel Extreme Value Distribution
content: gumbel(loc=0.0, scale=1.0): Right-skewed extreme value distribution. f(x) = exp[−x − e^(−x)]. Models maxima of N samples following Fisher-Tippett-Gnedenko extreme-value laws.
engine_application: Longest Completion, Longest Reception, Longest Rush prop pricing (maxima of N plays follow extreme-value laws, never Gaussian/Poisson)

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Weibull Extreme Value Distribution
content: weibull(a): Extreme-value distribution. f(x; c) = a·x^(a−1)·exp(−x^a)·I(0,∞)(x). Used for modeling minima/maxima and failure times.
engine_application: Longest Rush and other extreme-value prop pricing

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Wald Inverse Gaussian Distribution
content: wald(µ, λ): Also called inverse Gaussian. If X is wald then λ(X−µ)²/(µ²X) is square of standard normal (chi-square with 1 df). pdf: f(x) = √(λ/(2πx³))·e^(−λ(x−µ)²/(2µ²x)). Models first-passage time of Brownian motion with drift.
engine_application: Time-to-Throw vs Pass-Rush Time-to-Pressure survival curves (@PattonAnalytics Pressure-to-Sack curve)

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Von Mises Circular Distribution
content: vonmises(µ, κ, size=None): Continuous distribution for circular attributes (angles, time of day). Mean direction µ, concentration κ. Small κ tends to uniform over [−π, π]. Large κ tends to normal with mean µ and variance 1/κ. f(x) = e^(κcos(x−µ)) / (2π·I₀(κ)) · I[−π,π](x).
engine_application: Wind-angle dispersion for Kicking Suite (FG Made, Total Kicking Points) and Deep Pass (20+ Air Yards) weather overlays

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: ogrid and ix_ Zero-Stride Broadcast Grids
content: ogrid: Open grid similar to mgrid but returns open grid to save space and time. Broadcasting rules ensure ufunc acts as if ogrid were mgrid result. ix_: Construct indexing arrays for cross-product of N 1-dimensional arrays. Default indexing does not do cross-product.
engine_application: Multi-Leg SGP Copula Joint Tail Evaluator: 3-leg, 4-leg, 5-leg SGP joint distributions with O(N) memory instead of O(Nᵈ) dense meshgrids

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: C-API GIL-Free Threading
content: Chapter 11 covers C-API extensions. NPY_BEGIN_ALLOW_THREADS / nogil=True enable GIL-free multi-threaded execution over contiguous C buffers with zero Python object references (PyDataType_REFCHK == 0).
engine_application: All 14 Week 8 games (24,500,000 total snaps) run concurrently across all CPU cores
code_equivalent: nogil=True / ThreadPoolExecutor over contiguous C buffers

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: PyArray_RemoveSmallest Stride Ordering
content: PyArray_IterAllButAxis and PyArray_RemoveSmallest (p. 268, 307-308): Ensure N_SIMS = 10,000 world axis is always innermost contiguous dimension (stride = itemsize) so SIMD AVX2/AVX-512 instructions process 8-16 worlds per CPU clock cycle.
engine_application: SIMD-optimized inner-dimension stride ordering for 10,000-world simulation axis

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: arctan2 hypot Directional Statistics
content: arctan2(x1, x2): Element-wise arc tangent of x1/x2 choosing quadrant correctly. hypot(x1, x2): sqrt(x1² + x2²) without overflow. angle(z): angle of complex number. Used with unwrap for continuous directional statistics.
engine_application: OpenCV route/rush angle computation and stadium wind vector magnitude

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: Linear Algebra SVD lstsq Cutoff
content: linalg module: norm, det, inv, pinv, solve, eig, eigh, eigvals, eigvalsh, lstsq, cholesky, svd. SVD cutoff for lstsq regularization. Special functions: i0.
engine_application: Tensor coupling solver regularization and least-squares fitting for tendency estimation

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: convolve and correlate Window Functions
content: convolve(a, v, mode): Discrete linear convolution. correlate(a, v, mode): Cross-correlation. Figure 5.1 shows windowing functions and time/frequency-domain behavior. Prolate-spheroidal windows maximize main-lobe energy vs side-lobe ringing; Kaiser is good approximation.
engine_application: FIR filtering of coaching tendency time series with side-lobe suppression

author: Travis E. Oliphant, PhD
title: C-API Array Method Alternative API
content: PyArray_GetField equivalent to self.getfield(dtype, offset). Return new array of given dtype using data in current array at specified byte offset. Same shape and strides as original array. Zero-copy field extraction for record arrays.
engine_application: Zero-copy field access on SNAP_TENSOR_DTYPE records across HoloMQ shared memory
